transcript.text: Hi, the light in my Neff oven has stopped working (model B1ACE4HN0B). Oven works fine otherwise. Can I change the bulb myself and what bulb do I need?

Yes, this is usually a homeowner job: with the oven completely cool, switch it off at the cooker isolator (not just the controls), then remove the glass lamp cover and unscrew the bulb. Use an oven-rated bulb, typically an SES/E14 small screw fitting rated to 300°C, but confirm the voltage and wattage from the old bulb or the markings inside the lamp cover before buying one—do not fit an ordinary household bulb. Wear gloves or use a cloth if the glass cover is tight, and do not force it.

Thanks, I'll isolate it at the cooker switch and let it cool first. The glass cover came off fine with a rubber glove, and the old bulb says E14, 25W, 300C. The filament looks broken. Is that the right replacement to buy?

The visibly broken filament makes the bulb by far the most likely cause, especially as the oven is otherwise working. Use a proper oven-rated E14/SES 300°C lamp, rather than a normal household E14 bulb. If the light still does not work after fitting it, the remaining likely causes are the lamp holder or its local wiring, which would need an engineer to inspect.
